Following yesterday's release of public betas for macOS 27, iPadOS 27, iOS 27, and other updates announced at WWDC26, Apple is now rolling out the first public betas for AirPods Max 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods (4th generation). Details below.

First batch of AirPods public firmware betas now available

Apple announced several new AirPods features last month at WWDC26, set to arrive alongside iOS 27 and other upcoming operating system updates.

These include customisable EQ personalisation controls for AirPods audio, as well as expanded GymKit support allowing AirPods Pro 3 users to sync heart rate data via iPhone.

Apple is also offering a firmware beta for AirPods Max 2 for the first time, requiring enrolment through a device running iOS 27 or macOS 27.

Following yesterday's release of the first public betas for iOS 27 and Apple's other upcoming operating systems, the company has now launched the first public beta firmware updates for the following AirPods models:

  • AirPods Max 2
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2
  • AirPods Pro 2 (USB-C)
  • AirPods (4th generation)
  • AirPods (4th generation, Active Noise Cancellation)

AirPods firmware version 9.0.314 has a build number of 9A5314b, identical to last week's developer beta.

Installing AirPods firmware beta

Below is Apple's official guidance on enrolling eligible AirPods in the firmware beta programme:

Enable beta updates. For Mac computers running macOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your Mac via Bluetooth settings. Go to System Settings > Bluetooth and click the (i) next to your AirPods. In the AirPods settings menu, scroll down to find "AirPods Beta Updates" and use the toggle to enable beta software updates. For iPhone and iPad running iOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your iOS device. Go to Settings > Bluetooth and tap the (i) next to your AirPods. Apple notes that once users toggle on "AirPods Beta Updates," the "firmware update will be installed automatically when the AirPods are in their charging case and near the paired iPhone or Mac".
